title: A smile is charity
hook: even meeting your brother with a cheerful face is charity (Tirmidhi)

segments.voice: Yesterday: ikhtilaf, scholars who differ, on music and on tattoos. Your line was where scholars differ, ask why.

Charity usually sounds like money. A donation page. A jar by the register. A fundraiser with a thermometer drawing that never quite fills up. If you don't have much money, it can feel like charity is for other people. Some poor companions said as much. Sahih Muslim reports they came to the Prophet ﷺ and complained: the wealthy are getting all the reward. They pray like us, they fast like us, and then they give from their extra money, and we can't. His answer widened the word.
screen: `CHARITY SOUNDS LIKE MONEY.` → `THE WEALTHY GET ALL THE REWARD.` → `HIS ANSWER WIDENED THE WORD.`

segments.voice: He told them: hasn't Allah given you things to give? Every glory to Allah is charity. Every praise is charity. Every Allahu akbar is charity. Telling someone about good is charity. The word is sadaqah, and its root is the surprising part: Lane's dictionary lists it under s-d-q, the root of sidq, truthfulness, and siddiq, the truthful. A hadith in Muslim calls sadaqah a proof, and commentators read it as faith showing it is true, faith with its hands out. In everyday use, zakat names the fixed yearly charity, which comes later this week, and sadaqah everything else: voluntary, any size, any time. And the hadith make everything else very wide. Bukhari reports: every good deed is sadaqah. Tirmidhi reports the Prophet ﷺ saying: your smile in the face of your brother is sadaqah. Pointing a lost person the right way is sadaqah. Pouring water from your bucket into someone else's is sadaqah. Sahih Muslim adds: don't think little of any good deed, even meeting your brother with a cheerful face. It even says every joint in the body owes a charity each day the sun rises, and that helping a man lift his bags onto his mount pays one. So the poor companions had plenty to give after all: a face, a word, directions, a little water. The Qur'an protects the heart of it, too. Surah al-Baqarah says: A kind word with forgiveness is better than almsgiving followed by injury. A smile given freely can be worth more than a check handed over with a sneer. In these hadith, charity isn't a special occasion. It's a way of turning your face.
screen: `THE POOR COMPANIONS COMPLAIN.` · `SADAQAH — FROM THE ROOT OF TRUTH.` · `YOUR SMILE IN YOUR BROTHER'S FACE.` · `A KIND WORD, BETTER THAN ALMS WITH INJURY.` · then, large: `A FACE CAN GIVE.`

segments.voice: Picture the first person you'll see after this, and let your face soften as you meet their eyes: not a forced grin, just warmth. Then someone you tend to ignore, a cashier, a driver, a cleaner, and then someone who's difficult for you, noticing where your face tightens and letting it ease. If you pray, you can intend each smile as sadaqah.
Sadaqah. Voluntary charity, from the root of truth: any good given freely, even a cheerful face. Today's word.
Your line: a face can give. The poor companions had more to give than they thought. See you tomorrow.

screen: `DAY 149 COUNTS.` → `TOMORROW: CHARITY FROM THE RIGHT HAND.`
